text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a chronic cough and a history of recurrent bronchitis; to determine the underlying cause, please tell me your age and how many years you have had the cough.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

Based on your history of recurrent bronchitis and the specific description of your sputum as "copious," "thick," "foamy," and "yellow-green," combined with the chronic nature of the cough (11 years) and morning exacerbations, this clinical picture strongly suggests bronchiectasis rather than simple chronic bronchitis. This is a condition where the bronchial tubes become permanently damaged and widened. To confirm this, I need to see the structural changes in your airways. Please hold while I request your chest imaging.
